title: Saft launches solid-state production lines in France – Batteries International
content: TotalEnergies-owned Saft has launched new production lines for solid-state batteries at its plant in France. The company said on October 19 the Bordeaux site will make Saft the first French manufacturer with the capacity to develop and produce solid-state batteries that use both sulfide and polymer electrolytes at room temperature. Saft did not disclose production capacities or investment costs, but said the technological combination offered increased safety in addition to energy density that is up to 50% higher than that of standard lithium ion batteries. The batteries are produced using a dry electrode process that Saft said is more environmentally responsible, claiming the process cuts CO 2 emissions from this stage of production by up to 40%. CEO Cedric Duclos said solid-state batteries are among the most promising innovations for meeting next-gen electrification needs. “These new production lines mark an important milestone for Saft, as we turn several years of research into real industrial capacity, a statement of our ambition to establish France and Europe as leading players in this strategic technology.” The announcement followed Saft’s October 6 confirmation that it had signed two contracts with Axpo, Switzerland’s largest producer of renewable energy, for the delivery of battery energy storage systems in France. Batteries International reported earlier this year that Saft planned to jointly develop next-gen sodium ion batteries under an agreement with Mana Battery. The firms announced on August 4 the agreement included validating the technology and paving the way for commercialisation — expanding cooperation on technical evaluation that began last year. Target markets for the collaboration include those such as defence and industry, which are already sectors served by lithium ion products from Saft. title: Japan’s GSA opens Swiss lab for next-gen battery recycling – Batteries International
content: Japanese chemical and green tech company Green Science Alliance has opened a laboratory dedicated to next-generation battery recycling in Switzerland. The lab, opened on October 19 at the Switzerland Innovation Park Biel/Bienne, operates in partnership with the Swiss Battery Technology Center. Work at the innovation park includes assessing regenerated materials, making electrodes and cells, testing performance, and evaluating industrial potential and scalability. GSA-developed materials for a more sustainable society include biomass-based alternatives to petroleum-derived products to rechargeable batteries, fuel cells and solar cells. GSA said it chose the Swiss site as its base for expanding in Europe and plans further collaborative R&D. The company aims to commercialise its technology in Europe with the help of the innovation park’s network of industrial partners, start-ups and research institutions across the battery value chain. If scaled up, the method could reduce the resources needed for recycling, lessen reliance on newly mined raw materials and support more resilient European battery supply chains, GSA said. Mechanically processing used lithium ion batteries produces a dark powder called black mass, which contains valuable electrode materials. Conventional recycling dissolves it with acids or bases to recover individual metals, which then need several more processing steps before reuse. GSA said its approach is to directly regenerate the cathode active materials so that they can go back into new batteries, without fully breaking them down into elements. This could cut recycling steps and resource use. Early results show that batteries made with regenerated cathode materials reached over 90% of the initial capacity of comparable batteries using commercial materials. title: Samsung SDI Signs 1-GWh ESS Deal, Expands Indiana Storage Push
content:
Battery News
Stationary Batteries
Battery Manufacturing
The agreement with Alpha Omega Power will be built at Kokomo's StarPlus Energy plant — a facility whose ownership future remains unresolved even as Samsung SDI leans harder into ESS.
October 26, 2026
4 Min Read
StarPlus Energy plant in Kokomo, IN.
Commercial Contracting Corporation
At a Glance
Samsung SDI and Alpha Omega Power sign a 1 GWh ESS supply deal, bringing their total agreements to 1.5 GWh.
The batteries will be built at Samsung SDI's StarPlus Energy plant in Kokomo, Indiana, using NCA prismatic cells.
The deal underscores Samsung SDI's pivot toward energy storage in Indiana as U.S. EV battery demand slows.
Samsung SDI is deepening its bet on US energy storage, announcing a
1 GWh supply agreement with Alpha Omega Power
(AOP), a utility-scale battery storage developer and independent power producer. Combined with an initial contract signed late last year, the two companies' agreements now total 1.5 GWh — all of it to be built at Samsung SDI's StarPlus Energy (SPE) plant in Kokomo, Indiana.
AOP plans to deploy the systems for large-scale projects in the WECC and ERCOT power markets, two regions where utilities and independent power producers are racing to add storage capacity to firm up renewables integration and meet surging demand tied to data centers and electrification. Construction is scheduled to begin next year.
The battery technology behind the deal
The agreement centers on Samsung SDI's Battery Box (SBB) 1.7, a fully integrated ESS solution built around high-nickel nickel cobalt aluminum (NCA) prismatic cells. The company says SBB 1.7 delivers 17% higher energy density than its predecessor, SBB 1.5, while keeping the same 20-foot footprint, and incorporates AI-driven algorithms for anomaly detection and battery life prediction across a 25-year design life. On the safety side, the system has secured NFPA 855 and UL 9540 certification and uses Samsung SDI's proprietary Enhanced Direct Injection technology, which pumps fire-suppressant directly into individual battery modules rather than relying on broader enclosure-level suppression.
Related:
Battery Breaking-News Headlines
Samsung SDI's Battery Box (SBB) 1.7. Credit: Samsung SDI
Samsung SDI is positioning the deal as proof of its differentiated standing in the market: the company says it remains the only non-Chinese supplier of prismatic ESS batteries in North America, and it is leaning on that distinction — along with prismatic cells' reputed durability and fire safety advantages over pouch-type designs — to win business from US developers facing increasingly strict safety requirements. "American-made ESS from SAMSUNG SDI will play an important role in AOP's continued growth," stated Paul Choi, CEO of Alpha Omega Power. Fabrice Hudry, President of the ESS Team at SAMSUNG SDI America, added that the company intends to "continue to expand our business foundation and strengthen our position in the North American ESS market" through its differentiated technology and local production.
Two Indiana plants have two different stories
The AOP agreement also offers a useful opportunity to clarify a point of potential confusion in Samsung SDI's Indiana footprint, since the company now operates two separate facilities in the state with very different ownership histories.
Related:
Michigan's Battery Bet Isn't Over Yet, Whitmer Tells Industry Leaders
StarPlus Energy, the Kokomo plant that will manufacture the AOP order, was founded in 2022 as a joint venture between Samsung SDI and Stellantis, originally intended to produce NCA lithium-ion EV batteries. As Battery Technology has previously reported, Stellantis was said in February 2026 to be exploring an exit from that venture amid more than €22 billion in company-wide losses tied to its EV strategy, and as of Samsung SDI's August 2026 statements, discussions over the future of StarPlus Energy remained ongoing with no resolution confirmed. Whether that ownership question has since been settled is not publicly clear. (bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-02-10/stellantis-seeks-to-exit-battery-venture-with-samsung-as-ev-losses-mount; electrive.com/2026/02/12/stellantis-likely-to-withdraw-from-battery-joint-venture-with-samsung-sdi; reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/stellantis-seeks-exit-battery-venture-with-samsung-ev-losses-mount-bloomberg-2026-02-10)
New Carlisle's SynergyCells plant has already changed hands
Kokomo is distinct from SynergyCells, the $3.5 billion, 27-GWh plant in New Carlisle, Indiana, that was previously a Samsung SDI–GM joint venture. As covered in
Battery Technology
's August 2026 feature,
Samsung SDI acquired GM's full 49.99% stake in that project
, making New Carlisle the company's first wholly owned North American cell site. Samsung SDI said at the time it would use the plant to "proactively respond to the fast-growing ESS market in the U.S.," even as it and GM separately agreed to co-develop next-generation prismatic EV cells for potential future use there. (batterytechonline.com/automotive-mobility/gm-exits-samsung-sdi-battery-venture-as-ohio-ultium-plant-restarts-production)
Related:
As Energy Storage Demand Explodes, The Battery Show North America Delivers Industry's Most Comprehensive Showcase
Taken together, the two moves describe a broader pattern: automaker partners stepping back from Indiana capacity originally earmarked for EV batteries, while Samsung SDI redirects that same manufacturing base toward stationary storage. That shift tracks with the wider slowdown in U.S. EV demand following the elimination of the federal $7,500 consumer tax credit in September 2025, which has pressured automakers and battery makers alike to rethink capacity commitments built for a faster EV ramp than materialized.
A pivot playing out industry-wide
Samsung SDI's Indiana reshuffling is not happening in isolation. GM has simultaneously revived its Ohio Ultium plant even as it exited the SynergyCells venture, and Ford and Stellantis have each been recalibrating their own U.S. battery manufacturing strategies this year. Against that backdrop, energy storage has emerged as the more reliable near-term growth market, driven by grid reliability needs, renewables buildout, and demand growth in markets like WECC and ERCOT that is less exposed to the policy volatility that has hit EV adoption.
Samsung SDI said it has secured a series of ESS supply deals with U.S. energy companies this year and is in discussions with additional customers, suggesting the AOP agreement is unlikely to be its last in the region. For a company now operating two large Indiana facilities with overlapping but distinct histories, the challenge going forward may be less about winning ESS contracts — demand for which appears robust — and more about resolving the ownership questions still hanging over at least one of those plants.

title: 7 Electric Motorcycles Worth a Look in 2026
content:
Automotive & Mobility
Design & Manufacturing
As major motorcycle brands went electric this year and smaller brands cut prices to compete, prospective riders now have plenty of strong models to choose from.
October 26, 2026
7 Slides
Start slideshow
The Can-Am Pulse.
For most of the past two decades, electric motorcycles were not a viable option for most consumers. The main problem was that only small specialty manufacturers produced them. Large motorcycle manufacturers stayed out of the game and relegated their electric efforts to scooters and concept bikes.
As a result, many electric motorcycles from small companies had high prices, limited range, slow charging, and thin dealer networks. To make matters worse, several of these producers ran out of money before they could perfect their motorbikes.
Fortunately, recent years have seen motorcycle designers resolve many of the problems that plagued older models. For example, they began building liquid-cooled batteries to improve energy density and make the battery packs a structural part of the chassis to save weight. Designers also began adding Combined Charging System (CCS) connectors used by electric cars so riders could use public fast chargers on longer trips.
Related:
Rivian Adds Ghostbusters-Themed Trick Or Treat Mode To R1 & R2 Electric Vehicles For Halloween
This year, many large manufacturers used these innovations to produce their own electric motorcycles. Honda put its first full-size electric motorcycle in European dealerships over the summer, and Royal Enfield began delivering its first electric bike in June. Those launches put electric motorcycles behind large dealer and service organizations, which the specialists have struggled to build. Riders who skipped older electric motorcycles because of range, charging time, or price now have their pick of models that deliver on all three.
We've put together a list of seven electric motorcycles worth riding in 2026. Read on to learn about each one's batteries, range, and price.

title: Leidos Brings AI to Pentagon Asset Management
content:
Leidos Brings AI to Pentagon Asset Management
Prioritise Us
on Google
Leidos will deploy AI-driven automation, cloud technology and modern software practices across the Pentagon’s ELMS under a potential US$95m, five-year contract from the DLA.
Leidos Senior Vice President Jason McCarthy explains how AI will modernise Pentagon asset management through a potential $95m DLA contract
Leidos will deploy AI-driven automation, cloud technology and modern software practices across the Pentagon’s Enterprise Logistics Management System (ELMS) under a potential US$95m, five-year contract from the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA).
ELMS is used by more than 50 government agencies to manage over 80 million items of government property valued at more than US$140bn. The system supports asset accountability throughout the property lifecycle and underpins the logistics network that helps keep US warfighters equipped and ready.
The contract extends Leidos’ support for ELMS and its predecessor, the Defense Property Accountability System, to more than 21 years. The agreement includes one base year and four option years, running through August 2031.
Leidos will bring AI advances to the Pentagon's logistics system under a $95 million contract. Credit: Getty
AI modernises Pentagon asset management
Leidos will apply AI automation to accelerate software delivery and streamline the processes supporting ELMS. The company will also use cloud capabilities and modern software development practices to support secure and reliable system operations.
The award forms part of Leidos’ NorthStar 2030 strategy, which focuses on applying advanced technology to national-security and defence missions. In this case, the technology is directed at a large-scale property and logistics system rather than a frontline weapons platform.
The planned improvements will focus on AI-driven automation for logistics and asset-management workflows; cloud technology supporting system operations and scalability; modern software development to accelerate delivery of system improvements; and secure ELMS operations for defence and government users.
In July, Leidos announced that it was partnering with Rune Technologies to combine Rune’s AI-enabled predictive logistics and sustainment mission command software with Leidos’ AI-enabled decision advantage and course-of-action generation capabilities.
The contract announcement did not quantify a direct impact on military performance, and Leidos has not disclosed the specific AI models, cloud architecture or individual workflows that will be automated.
The Military Sealift Command (MSC) Combat Logistics Force (CLF) fleet replenishment oiler USNS Patuxent (T-AO 201) returns to Naval Station Norfolk, 10 December 2024. (U.S. Navy photo by Ryan Carter)
Defence logistics and military readiness
ELMS helps the Department of War manage and account for assets throughout their lifecycle. The system’s scope covers government property valued at more than US$140bn and used across more than 50 agencies.
Accurate asset records are important to defence logistics because they help organisations understand where equipment is located, how it is being used and what support or replacement actions may be required. Better visibility can contribute to planning, maintenance, inventory control and operational readiness.
Kevin Quarderer, director of International Science and Technology at Leidos, writing in US services magazine Stars and Stripes in August, explained that “the particular challenges of military logistics will require commanders to support distributed forces using a mix of military, allied and commercial networks that often lack seamless integration or shared visibility.”
“Autonomous systems, predictive analytics, and resilience communications can extend reach and reduce risk, but only if integrated into a coherent logistics architecture designed to absorb shocks and adapt under pressure,” Kevin concluded.
“Logistics wins wars and accurate, reliable asset visibility is a cornerstone of military readiness. This is Leidos defence technology in action, applying modern tools to help DLA strengthen the digital backbone of defence logistics,” Jason McCarthy, Senior Vice President, Airborne & Mission Solutions, Leidos.
The statement positions ELMS modernisation as a readiness initiative as well as an information-technology programme. Improving the speed, reliability and security of asset-management processes could support decision-making across the defence logistics enterprise.
Leidos extends 21-year ELMS relationship
The DLA award extends Leidos’ long-running role supporting ELMS and its predecessor system. The company says its involvement will exceed 21 years when the new contract period is included.
The continuity is significant because modernising a mission-critical logistics platform requires knowledge of existing processes, data structures, users and security requirements. Leidos’ established support role may help reduce transition risk while new automation and cloud capabilities are introduced.
The contract’s principal data points are:
Contract customer: Defense Logistics Agency
Contractor: Leidos
Potential value: US$95m
Duration: Five years
Structure: One base year plus four option years
End date: August 2031
System: Enterprise Logistics Management System
User base: More than 50 government agencies
Assets managed: More than 80 million items
Asset value: More than $140bn
Leidos support history: More than 21 years
The US$95m figure is the contract’s total potential value. Because four years are structured as option periods, the full amount depends on the exercise of those options.
Leidos’ NorthStar 2030 strategy
Leidos is linking the DLA award to its NorthStar 2030 strategy. The company presents the strategy as a framework for delivering mission-ready technology across defence, government and national-security markets.
The ELMS contract gives Leidos an opportunity to apply that strategy to a high-value government logistics platform. It also demonstrates how AI adoption in defence can involve administrative and operational systems, not only intelligence, surveillance, weapons or autonomous platforms.
The programme’s success will depend on whether automation improves software delivery and logistics processes without reducing system reliability or accountability. The scale of the ELMS means that changes must work across diverse government users and a large asset base.

title: BYD opens pre-orders for its first luxury electric SUV with over 1,000 km CLTC range
content:
Peter Johnson
| Oct 26 2026 - 7:36 am PT
opened pre-orders for the new Denza N8, a luxury five-seat electric SUV with a CLTC range of over 1,000 km (621 miles).
BYD Denza N8 orders open with 1,003 km of CLTC range
“The king of large 5-seater pure electric vehicles,” as BYD’s luxury sub-brand Denza calls it, is now available to pre-order in China.
BYD opened pre-orders for the new Denza N8 on Monday, and the results so far “have been excellent,” according to Li Hui, Denza’s general manager.
The new Denza N8 is “definitely the most anticipated luxury SUV of the year,” Li said. Denza confirmed in August that the new version will use its Blade Battery 2.0 and Flash Charging Technology to deliver “a world-leading 1,003 km pure electric range.”
Although BYD has released several luxury EVs that offer more than 1,000 km of CLTC range, such as
the Denza Z9 GT
, this is its first electric SUV to break the 1,000 km mark under CLTC conditions.
BYD Denza N8 (Source: Denza)
For context, the plug-in hybrid version the new Denza N8 is replacing offered a combined CLTC range of 1,003 km (623 miles) on a full tank of gas and a full charge.
BYD didn’t reveal pre-order prices, but Li confirmed last week that the
Denza N8’s official launch
is scheduled for November.
It will go on sale after the new Denza N8L, a slightly longer six-seat version. The N8L is available in two versions: Premium and Flagship. The N8L EV Premium starts at 299,800 RMB, or about $45,000, while the Flagship model is priced from 329,800 RMB ($49,000).
Denza N8 EV interior (Source: Denza)
Those who place a reservation with a 2,000 RMB ($200) deposit will receive a 5,000 RMB credit as a limited-time special offer.
Measuring 5,150 mm long, 1,999 mm wide, and 1,820 mm high, with a 3,075 mm wheelbase, the Denza N8 EV is slightly longer than the Kia EV9 and Hyundai IONIQ 9.
Inside, the five-seat electric SUV features a massive 30″ infotainment screen that spans nearly the entire passenger-side dashboard, plus a new 43″ (1.1 meter) panoramic head-up display (PHUD) at the bottom of the windshield.
Other premium features include zero gravity seating in all rows, a three-spoke steering wheel, wireless phone chargers, and ambient lighting.
The luxury SUV is equipped with a roof-mounted LiDAR to support BYD’s God’s Eye 5.0 smart driving assistance system. It also features DiSus-A, BYD’s intelligent air suspension system, and rear-wheel drive.
The new Denza N8 EV will be available with a single rear-wheel-drive (RWD) or a tri-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain. The RWD version uses a single motor producing either 320 kW (429 hp) or 370 kW (496 hp).
BYD’s new Denza N8 and N8L CLTC driving range, battery specs, and more (Source: China MIIT)
The tri-motor Denza N8 uses BYD’s e3 platform. The setup includes a 270 kW (362 hp) front motor and two 310 kW (416 hp) rear motors, delivering a combined output of 890 kW (1,193 hp).
Regulatory filings earlier this year revealed it will be available with a 130.15 kWh or 105.79 kWh BYD Blade 2.0 battery, offering CLTC ranges of up to 1,003 km and 800 km, respectively.
BYD will announce prices next month, but given that the Denza N8L starts at 299,800 RMB ($45,000), the standard version will likely be priced below it.

title: Volkswagen gets L3 autonomous driving test permit in China, eyes 2027
content:
Volkswagen
Volkswagen Group
self-driving
Fred Lambert
| Oct 26 2026 - 6:59 am PT
VW Brand CEO Thomas Schäfer introduces the ID. EVERY1 concept car (Source: Volkswagen)
Volkswagen Group China now has a permit to test Level 3 autonomous driving on public roads in Hefei, and it says testing is already underway. The permit also covers large-scale driving data collection in the city.
It’s the latest step toward VW’s goal of L3 technology readiness in China by 2027. And the timing is good as the group holds its first China Technology Day in Hefei on Wednesday.
VW’s China autonomy stack
VW says the permit was issued under China’s strictest L3 framework and that its setup meets the country’s latest mandatory safety design standards. It didn’t say which authority issued it, how many vehicles are in the fleet, or which roads they can use.
Hefei makes sense as a base. It’s home to the Volkswagen China Technology Company (VCTC), the group’s largest R&D center outside Germany, and to its Volkswagen Anhui production site.
The software comes from CARIZON, VW’s intelligent driving unit in China, which started as a joint venture between CARIAD and Horizon Robotics. Its driver assistance system is called Hyper Sense 8 (HS8), which VW describes as its first “full-scenario” ADAS.
Behind it is GAIA 2.0, a world model VW built itself. VW says it runs simulation equal to 5 million km of safety testing per day, using about 30 million real-road scenario clips, and it wants to get that to 10 million km per day. VW is also developing its own system-on-chip, the C7H, which it says can support up to Level 4.
Ralf Brandstätter, chairman and CEO of Volkswagen Group China, kept the message on safety. He said the group “will never advance technology at the cost of safety” and called the permit an important step on the road to L3 readiness (our translation from Chinese).
A test permit, not a product launch
This is a road test permit. VW can’t sell L3 cars to customers with it.
China’s MIIT granted the country’s first L3 product approvals in December 2025 to two sedans: a Changan model capped at 50 km/h on designated Chongqing expressways, and a BAIC Arcfox model capped at 80 km/h on three Beijing routes. GAC’s Hyptec and XPeng already hold L3 road test permits too. So VW isn’t leading here. It’s catching up to Chinese brands on their home turf.
In July, VW, CARIZON, and Horizon Robotics said they would deepen their partnership, giving CARIZON “white-box” access to Horizon’s AI foundation model, and targeted the start of L3 deliveries in the second half of 2027. VW’s L2++ system is rolling out on seven new NEV models from its Chinese joint ventures this year.
VW also leans on XPeng in China. It bought a
roughly 5% stake in XPeng in 2023
and co-developed its China zonal electrical architecture, CEA, with the startup.
Outside China, the only Western automaker with a certified L3 system on sale is Mercedes-Benz, whose
Drive Pilot
works on approved highways in Germany and in California and Nevada. Mercedes also
got approval to test Level 4 driving in Beijing
back in 2024. Tesla’s FSD remains a Level 2 system everywhere it’s sold, China included.
Electrek’s Take
L3 is where liability moves. When the system is engaged, the automaker is responsible for the driving, not the person in the seat. That’s why so few companies have shipped it, and why the ones that have keep it on a short leash: specific roads, low speeds, mostly traffic jams.
China has been serious about building a framework for automakers to bring this techonology to market, and through it, we are seeing who is interested in this version of autonomy.
Not everyone is. Many automakers, including Tesla, have been talking about “skipping” level 3 and going straight to level 4.

title: Range Energy shows how its eTrailer saves almost as much as a Tesla Semi
content:
Range Energy, a company working to electrify trucking through the use of a trailer with its own battery and motors, has published an analysis showing how much fleets can save through electrification – and just at the right time, with diesel at record highs.
You may have heard a little something about diesel prices lately, which have just about doubled in less than a year due to Donald Trump’s war of choice in Iran.
Diesel is now at record highs, and it’s devastating fleets and truck drivers and anyone who uses any products that are delivered on trucks (so, everyone). It’s an urgent problem that needs an urgent solution, and solutions are not forthcoming from the responsible entities.
So, fleets have to seek another solution, and Range Energy would like to be the one that provides it.
Range is a startup based in California, founded and staffed by former Tesla employees and others from around the EV industry. It’s building an electrified trailer which we demoed at ACT Expo in 2024 (really, watch it, it’s a very cool demo) which promises to cut fleet fuel use significantly.
It does this by having its own battery and motors inside the trailer, meaning the tractor doesn’t have to work nearly as hard as the trailer can effectively pull its own weight. Even though the tractor still runs on diesel, it uses a whole lot less of it.
This differs from the other popular option for fleets: full electrification. There are a number of electric semi tractors available, and fleets have been moving to install them, getting their depots ready for charging. But Range lets you bring your own tractor, and electrifies the trailer instead.
Range previously published some early findings, showing a 36% reduction in fuel use in a testing scenario. It also did a pilot program with an egg farm in California, which improved the fuel efficiency of the farm’s diesel fleet by 50-70%.
Now Range has published its own white paper showing comparative savings that fleets can achieve with either its own solution, the eTrailer, or Tesla’s solution, the fully electric Tesla Semi. The paper does not cover the various other electric semi tractors available on the market today, just a face-off between Range and Tesla.
The analysis goes through several scenarios, mostly focusing on refrigerated trailer units (“reefers”), which is the first product Range is focusing on.
Trailer electrification is a great idea for reefers, because they usually fill up on volume rather than weight (called “cubing out”), meaning battery weight doesn’t eat into maximum trailer payload. Batteries also offer power to run refrigeration, meaning you don’t need to have a diesel generator on the trailer.
The upshot of the whole thing is that: fleets can save money with the Range eTrailer, and can theoretically save more money with the Tesla Semi, but the numbers are relatively close in the most common scenario, and the Tesla scenarios have a much wider spread depending on what implementation you consider.
For example, if you only use public chargers rather than your own depot, the Tesla Semi will be more costly because energy will be more expensive to your fleet than if you bought it at commercial utility rates. So, even though installing chargers in your depot sounds expensive, it will pencil out better in the end.
The best money savings came from having two Semis share the same charger, but that requires tight timings and overnight driving.
Another important feature Range points out is build time for a project. The nice thing about the eTrailer is it can slot into fleets immediately with little operational change required, whereas the larger charging needs of an electric tractor) tend to require bigger projects to get a depot ready with chargers (but despite the higher upfront costs, you get better long-term savings, since you avoid diesel entirely with an electric tractor).
In the end, Range found that its solution saves a little more money than the Tesla Semi does in most scenarios, but the difference is quite narrow, with each option having its strengths and weaknesses. Both solutions are better than diesel in most scenarios, but not all of them.
You don’t necessarily need to choose between the two, as an electrified trailer can still be used with an electric tractor. It works the same way in either case – using its own motors to take some of the effort off the tractor. This means extended range, for longer hauls with light loads that couldn’t quite make it on the Tesla Semi’s inherent range. And the benefit of being able to run the reefer while disconnected from the tractor or shore power remains as well.
The analysis has plenty of limitations. It has to estimate future diesel costs (it used a number below current prices, but still historically high), didn’t cover financing costs, it doesn’t have real-world data for the Tesla Semi, didn’t cover electrified tractor or trailer options from other companies, can’t analyze individual charging costs site-to-site since each is specific to a utility company, didn’t cover the myriad incentives available in various regions, and most of all it didn’t consider diesel emissions, which are a huge societal cost to everyone that electrification reduces (and full electrification reduces more).
So in the end, every fleet has a different use case, and should run the numbers themselves to see how either solution would fit in. But in the generalized case, it looks like there are plenty of savings available out there, whether through tractor or trailer electrification.
Top comment by OliveMagnet
I’m not sure I understand their claims when compared to the Semi. Doesn’t the Semi have its own electric takeoff system to power reefers? That means the reefer would be running on the same cost/kWh as the Semi but without the added capex for solar, batteries etc.
I guess if they are only modeling Semi + diesel reefer it makes sense but seems logical fleet operators would power the reefer with the Semi electric takeoff system. In fact, I imagine trailer manufacturers would begin migrating from hybrid reefers to fully electric reefers, removing the diesel components and lowering trailer costs further.
Either way, seems like a great solution when paired with diesel tractors!
Unfortunately, given diesel prices are at record highs right now, both of the options in the paper are a little suboptimal. Tesla Semis have been on order for almost ten years now, and Tesla only just claimed it has started production in earnest. And Range is still about a year out from volume production of its eTrailer, which it says will start in late 2027 – so, while an eTrailer will be able to slot into a fleet immediately when it’s available, it’s not available yet, which puts a damper on that potential benefit.
So neither can offer immediate relief, but both offer good options for fleets to plan for the next inevitable oil shock – which is why Range didn’t base its analysis solely on current prices (remember, we just had another shock in 2022, this nonsense happens all the time, maybe it’s time to stop using oil). But, the numbers in the paper for the Tesla Semi can be compared to numbers for other electric tractors already available today, which can in turn be compared to the costs of the eTrailer, for fleets so inclined to make that comparison.

title: All aboard! Massachusetts is getting 10 new electric transit trains
content:
Electric train
Public Transit
Jo Borrás
| Oct 26 2026 - 4:42 am PT
The Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority (MBTA) board of directors voted unanimously Thursday to approve the purchase of a new generation of battery-powered public transit trains – and they can’t arrive soon enough.
“(MBTA) has, obviously, an immediate need for locomotives,”
explains William Wolfgang, the MBTA’s senior director of vehicle engineering
. The new machines will replace the oldest locomotives in the MBTA fleet, GP40s built more than 50 years ago and F40s that are well over 30 years old.
In a presentation to the MTBA board
, MTBA said 13 of the GP40s have, “exceeded their useful life,” while the F40s will reach the end of their life between 2029 and 2035.
The MBTA will put in an order for 20
Siemens-built
“Charger” locomotives; 10 Tier 4 diesel-powered hybrid electric units and 10 dual-mode battery/
catenary
electric units – and, beyond trackside power for charging the batteries, there are other challenges presented by going electric, most notably using existing cab cars to control the battery-electric units. “We’re going to have to work with railroad operations, engineering, and the Brotherhood of [
Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen
] to try and determine the best way to handle that,” adds Wolfgang. “That will be an upcoming change order once we get into the design review process.”
The total bill comes out to $310.4 million. A combination of state and federal funding will pay for the order,
including a recent $200 million transfer from the Massachusetts Department of Transportation
The contract includes an option for additional locomotives, although details were not discussed during the meeting. Delivery of the new Siemens Charger trains is set to begin in 2029, with all 20 set to be in service by the end of 2030. Siemens has delivered 440 Charger model hybrid- and battery-electric locomotives globally at the time of this writing.

title: Amflow launches two powerful new electric bikes, including its first SUV-style e-bike
content:
Micah Toll
| Oct 26 2026 - 1:01 am PT
Amflow, the electric bicycle brand that burst onto the scene with some of the most powerful and lightweight electric mountain bikes on the market, is expanding its lineup with two major releases. The company has announced global availability of its new Amflow TL Carbon, while also bringing its removable-battery Amflow PR Carbon series to the US for the first time.
Both models are powered by the latest Avinox mid-drive motor systems, which have quickly earned a reputation for delivering impressive power in surprisingly compact packages.
The biggest departure from
Amflow’s
roots is the new TL Carbon, which takes the company’s high-performance mountain biking DNA and applies it to a more versatile SUV-style electric bike. While less common in the US (ironically), SUV-style e-bikes are essentially a hybrid electric bicycle designed to act as an all-in-one, “do-it-all” vehicle combining the rugged build and off-road capability of an electric mountain bike with the practical, everyday utility of a city or trekking bike.
Rather than focusing exclusively on technical trails and aggressive mountain biking, the TL Carbon is designed to handle everything from daily commuting to touring and off-road adventures. And with Avinox’s RS800 battery featuring 800Wh of capacity, it’s got plenty of energy on board for diverse adventures.
The full-suspension bike uses the Avinox M2 motor, delivering up to 125 Nm of torque, which should provide more than enough grunt for steep climbs, heavy loads, and just about anything else riders can throw at it.
Avinox e-bike drive systems are known for many things, but chief among them is the
extremely high power and torque they offer
, eclipsing most other mid-drive motor systems on the market.
Despite that power and versatility, the TL Carbon weighs as little as 22.6 kg (49.8 lb). It also boasts an impressive maximum total weight capacity of 200 kg (441 lb), including the bike itself, rider, and cargo carried on its front and rear racks.
That’s a compelling combination for riders who want the performance of a premium electric mountain bike but need something practical enough to replace a car for everyday trips.
And perhaps most surprisingly, the price isn’t completely outrageous. The Amflow TL Carbon starts at $3,899 in the US and €3,499 in Germany, positioning it competitively against premium European trekking and SUV-style e-bikes.
Meanwhile, American riders are finally getting access to the Amflow PR Carbon series, which had previously launched in other markets.
Unlike Amflow’s earlier electric mountain bikes, the PR series features a removable battery, addressing one of the biggest practical complaints about high-performance eMTBs with integrated batteries.
The new 800 Wh battery weighs just 4 kg (8.8 lb) and can be removed for convenient indoor charging or swapped for a fresh battery to extend a ride. That’s especially useful for riders who don’t have a convenient charging outlet near their bike storage area.
Amflow claims up to 158 km (98 miles) of range under ideal conditions, though that’s based on relatively gentle riding on flat pavement in Eco mode. Riders tackling technical trails with high assistance levels should expect considerably less. But any way you slice it, 800 Wh is a huge battery for eMTBs and should deliver plenty of range under most conditions.
The standard PR Carbon uses the Avinox M2 motor with up to 125 Nm of torque, while the higher-end PR Carbon Pro upgrades to the more powerful Avinox M2S motor, producing up to 150 Nm of torque.
In the US, the PR Carbon starts at $4,999, while the PR Carbon Pro commands $6,799. European pricing starts at €4,499 and €5,899, respectively, based on German pricing.
All three bikes are available beginning today through ⁠Amflow’s official website and its network of authorized dealers. In the US, both models generally arrive as Class 1 e-bikes (no throttle) with a top speed of 20 mph (32 km/h), though Amflow models can typically be unlocked to Class 3 performance with a top speed of 28 mph (45 km/h).
Electrek’s Take
Amflow has been one of the more interesting brands to watch in the premium e-bike space, largely because of how aggressively it has pushed the boundaries of motor performance and bike weight.
But these latest releases show that the company is thinking beyond simply building increasingly powerful electric mountain bikes.
The TL Carbon is particularly interesting to me because it brings that impressive Avinox performance to a more practical platform. As someone who spends a minority of my riding time in the dirt, Amflow suddenly looks a lot more interesting to me, personally. Not everyone needs a dedicated eMTB, but plenty of riders would appreciate a lightweight, powerful, well-equipped electric bike that can handle both weekday commuting and weekend adventures.
And the PR Carbon’s removable battery is a welcome development, especially as the industry continues to recognize that convenience and serviceability matter just as much as outright performance.
With the Avinox ecosystem continuing to expand across more bike brands and categories, Amflow is also facing increasing competition from other manufacturers using the same impressive motors. That makes it all the more important for the brand to differentiate itself through thoughtful bike design, not just headline-grabbing power figures.

title: Xpanner launches automated pile driver to speed up utility-scale solar, energy storage installation - pv magazine Global
content:
Technology & Products
The fully automated system combines GNSS positioning and remote control operation to reduce pile driving cycle times by 45% on utility-scale solar and battery storage job sites.
Ryan Kennedy
26 Oct 2026
Technology & Products
Utility-scale
Construction automation company Xpanner announced the commercial launch of the X1 Piling R6, a fully automated pile driving machine engineered to accelerate civil installation timelines on utility-scale solar and battery energy storage system construction sites.
The system pairs Xpanner’s field-proven automation hardware and software stack with an Everstar R6 crawler base machine to automate pile positioning, travel, alignment, hammering, and depth control in a single execution cycle.
Conventional pile driving typically requires a two-person crew operating alongside separate surveying, marking, and site preparation teams. The X1 folds those manual steps into an automated workflow executed via remote control. Operators upload a pile schedule and coordinate file, guide the machine to the start of a row, and initiate operation with a single command.
High-precision dual-antenna GNSS receivers with Real-Time Kinematic support deliver centimeter-level positioning and orientation accuracy. Controlled by an onboard industrial controller operating on a real-time operating system, the system automatically navigates the crawler to each target location, aligns the mast, and drives piles to specified elevation and plumb tolerances without requiring personnel near the mast.
The underlying stack builds on Xpanner’s PD10 platform, which has been deployed across more than 67 U.S. job sites by major engineering, procurement, and construction contractors. Integrated on the Everstar R6 carrier, the X1 achieves a 45% faster cycle time compared to the previous generation, according to the company.
Machine specs and hydraulic capacity
Powered by a 130 horsepower engine operating at a maximum hydraulic pressure of 2,900 psi and a flow rate of 31.7 gallons per minute, the crawler features a high-frequency hydraulic hammer delivering up to 929 foot-pounds of impact energy. The hammer utilizes a 3.35-inch borer pole with three energy settings to adjust for varying soil resistance and geotechnical conditions.
To eliminate unnecessary machine movement on site, the carrier features fine-positioning capabilities. The guide rail slides 11.8 inches (300 mm) fore and aft, 19.7 inches (500 mm) laterally, and offers 180 degrees of upper-body rotation. The mast adjusts 10 degrees forward and backward, with a side tilt range from 7 degrees left to 64 degrees right, allowing operators to achieve target placement from a single setup position.
The system accommodates pile lengths up to 7.0 m with a maximum driving depth of 4.8 m. Because the hammer lowers near ground level and the guide rail plants vertically into the dirt during operation, the unit can drive piles flush to grade without adapters, handling standard tracker piles, short motor piles, and lower-profile BESS foundation piles on the same carrier chassis. Optional mast configurations support down-the-hole drilling, auger drilling with diameters ranging from 2.6 to 13.8 inches (66 to 350 mm), and ground screwing.
With an operating weight of 14,330 lb (6,500 kg), the carrier has compact transport dimensions of 3.7 m in length, 2.15 m in width, and 2.7 m in height. It is powered by a 130 hp (97 kW) engine and delivers a hammer impact energy of 929 ft·lb (1,260 J). The machine achieves a travel speed exceeding 1.6 mph (2.5 km/h) and can negotiate gradients of up to 20 degrees. Its tank capacities include 43.6 gallons of diesel fuel and 38.6 gallons of hydraulic oil.
“Solar and BESS builders are racing to bring new power online for the grid and for AI data centers, and they can’t find enough skilled crews to keep up,” said Henri Lee, co-founder and CEO of Xpanner. “X1 lets one operator drive every pile plumb with a single touch, keeps people away from the mast, and logs each pile as it goes in.”
Field controller hardware and cloud telemetry
On-site machine interaction relies on a 10.1-inch, sunlight-readable touch display built to handle extreme job site conditions, weather, and heavy vibration. The system is designed to operate reliably across extreme temperatures ranging from -40°F to 185°F.
The hardware connects to Xpanner Connect, a web-based project management dashboard that logs spatial coordinates, driving depth, and plumb status for each driven pile in real time. The live site map eliminates manual end-of-day reporting, offering remote fleet visibility into machine state, cycle metrics, and site progress.
The X1 Piling R6 is commercially available starting October 26, 2026, through an Automation-as-a-Service subscription model that bundles the crawler chassis, automation hardware, cloud software, site validation, and direct on-site support.

Inverters

title: Citicore secures $552 million for 900 MW solar, 120 MWh storage portfolio in Philippines - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Bank of the Philippine Islands, Land Bank of the Philippines and Development Bank of the Philippines have provided PHP 35.014 billion ($552 million) in financing for a portfolio of five solar projects totaling 900 MW and 120 MWh of battery storage in the Philippines.
Vincent Shaw
26 Oct 2026
Markets & Policy
Asia-Pacific
Utility-scale
A PV plant operated by Citicore in the Philippines
Philippine renewable energy developer Citicore Renewable Energy Corp. (CREC) has secured PHP 35.014 billion ($552 million) in syndicated project financing to develop five solar projects with a combined capacity of 900 MW and 120 MWh of battery storage in Batangas province.
The financing is the company’s largest syndicated loan facility to date. Three Philippine banks provided the funding: Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI), state-owned Land Bank of the Philippines (LandBank), and Development Bank of the Philippines (DBP).
The portfolio consists of two 300 MW solar plants and three 100 MW solar facilities. Each of the smaller projects will incorporate a 40 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS), bringing the portfolio’s total storage capacity to 120 MWh.
CREC has not disclosed the batteries’ power ratings, technology suppliers or storage durations. It has also not provided details of the loan tenor, interest rates or financing allocated to individual projects.
All five projects secured offtake allocations under the Philippine Department of Energy’s
fourth Green Energy Auction Program
(GEA-4), held in 2025.
The auction framework provides for 20-year electricity supply contracts starting from commercial operation, giving developers long-term revenue visibility. CREC has not disclosed the tariffs awarded to individual projects, commissioning schedules or the status of their power supply agreements.
The projects will expand CREC’s existing portfolio in Batangas, where it reports 374 MW of operational solar capacity and 560 MWh of battery storage. An additional 198 MW of solar capacity in the province is nearing completion.
CREC said concentrating multiple projects in Batangas is part of its development strategy, enabling it to coordinate construction activities and potentially improve project execution efficiency.
The Philippine government has used successive green energy auctions to accelerate renewable energy investment. The
fourth auction round
covered ground-mounted, rooftop and floating solar, onshore wind, and integrated solar-plus-storage projects, with electricity deliveries scheduled between 2026 and 2029.
The Philippines aims to increase the share of renewables in its electricity generation mix to 35% by 2030 and 50% by 2040.
CREC, which is listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange, operates across solar power generation, project development and electricity supply. The company said earlier in October that it had reached 1 GW of installed renewable energy capacity and is targeting 5 GW within the next five years.

content:

South Korean manufacturer’s Michigan-based subsidiary will supply Alpha Omega Power with utility-scale battery storage. The supply agreement covers Samsung SDI’s containerized nickel cobalt aluminum (NCA) cell-based solution, Samsung Battery Box 1.7.
Matthew Lynas
26 Oct 2026
Markets & Policy
Batteries
Energy Storage
Samsung SDI’s SBB 1.7 BESS uses cells with a high nickel NCA chemistry.
Samsung SDI has signed a deal to supply 1 GWh of nickel cobalt aluminum (NCA) battery storage to a single US customer, with all cells and modules to be manufactured in the United States.
Under the agreement with utility and independent power producer Alpha Omega Power (APO), Samsung SDI is expected to deliver its Samsung Battery Box (SBB) 1.7 containerized energy storage to projects scheduled to being construction in 2027. These will include projects in the Western Electricity Coordinating Council (WECC) and Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) energy markets.
All cells and modules for the battery containers covered in the supply agreement will be manufactured at Samsung SDI’s StarPlus Energy (SPE) plant in Kokomo, Indiana, according to the manufacturer, with delivery expected before the end of 2026.
In choosing Samsung SDI as a supplier, APO is putting significant investment into NCA chemistry battery storage in a global market where cells using lithium iron phosphate (LFP) based chemistry continue to lead. The investment also comes as the US government mulls further restrictions on imported power equipment.
Samsung SDI reports that the SBB 1.7 uses a high-nickel NCA chemistry and delivers 17% higher energy density than its predecessor, the SBB 1.5, while maintaining the same 20-foot footprint. The manufacturer also highlights fire safety as a key feature of the design, noting the battery storage solution incorporates Samsung SDI’s proprietary Enhanced Direct Injection technology, which directly injects fire-extinguishing agents into individual battery modules.
The latest agreement means Samsung SDI has been contracted to supply a total of 1.5 GWh of energy storage to APO, following an earlier supply contract signed in 2025.
In a press release, Fabrice Hudry president ESS of Samsung SDI America, said the company’s “differentiated technology” and US production capabilities will see it continue to expand in the North American ESS market.
Paul Choi, CEO of Alpha Omega Power, added: “American-made ESS from Samsung SDI will play an important role in AOP’s continued growth. This second agreement strengthens our domestic supply chain supporting the next generation of energy infrastructure.”

The Czech government has proposed changes to its new capacity mechanism, which is open to battery storage, including moving two supplementary auctions from 2026 to 2027, a year later than prospective participants had planned for.
Brian Publicover
26 Oct 2026
Markets & Policy
Energy Storage
Utility-scale
The Czech Ministry of Industry and Trade (MPO) has published a draft amendment to a general measure it issued in August introducing the country’s capacity mechanism. The draft also proposes a related obligation on Czech transmission system operator ČEPS.
The ministry said the changes are intended to clarify the mechanism’s conditions, strengthen legal certainty for participants, ensure transparent and nondiscriminatory procedures and adapt the rules to practical implementation. Anyone whose rights or interests may be directly affected can submit written comments until Oct. 30.
According to Czech energy news site
oEnergetice
, the draft changes 20 provisions of the original measure and moves two extraordinary supplementary auctions, held four and five years before delivery, from 2026 to 2027. The outlet reported that the draft also clarifies rules for extending the preliminary assessment, allows capacity eligible for 15-year contracts to compete in several auctions at the same time and changes how the demand curve is constructed.
Auction timeline
In September, ČEPS extended the preliminary assessment deadline for the first three auctions, the main auction and the two supplementary auctions, from Sept. 20 to Nov. 18, at the ministry’s request. The ministry cited conditions in the energy equipment market and supply chains and the aim of widening competition among future capacity providers.
The first delivery period runs from Nov. 1, 2030, to Oct. 31, 2031.
The European Commission approved the original mechanism on July 16 for 10 years, with an estimated budget of €3.1 billion ($3.5 billion) to €6.2 billion, financed through consumer charges. Individual contracts can last up to 15 years. Existing and new generation, electricity storage, cross-border capacity and demand-side response are eligible to participate.

title: Norwegian alliance calls for increased solar support - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Trade union, environmental and business organisations in Norway have signed a joint letter demanding the Norwegian government backs five measures to support the country’s solar industry.
Patrick Jowett
26 Oct 2026
Markets & Policy
Batteries
Commercial & industrial
Highlights
Residential
A coalition of 16 Norwegian companies have addressed a letter to the Norwegian parliament, known as the
Storting
, to support the country’s solar industry.
Led by Norway’s renewable industry and employer association, Fornybar Norge, the letter includes signatures from the country’s Building Materials Industry Association, Electrical and IT Association and Electricity Association, as well as its Nature Conservation Association and National Homeowners Association.
The letter explains Norway’s solar sector is far off the pace of deployment required to reach the
Storting
‘s goal of generating 8 TWh of solar power by 2030. It adds slow market growth has been compounded by “two tough years” of bankruptcies and layoffs in its domestic solar market.
“For every month without action, the industry loses the expertise needed to develop more clean power for climate action, construction and business development,” the letter reads. “Now a change of pace in solar investment is needed, combined with increased efforts for energy efficiency.”
It asks the Storting to focus on five measures for the solar industry as part of its ongoing budget negotiations for 2027.
These include introducing an auction-based support scheme for solar projects on commercial buildings and expanding sharing schemes so electricity generated from one rooftop PV array can be shared with neighbours, housing associations and nearby commercial buildings. Other measures include mandating solar panels on new buildings and major commercial buildings with a useable area of 500 sqm or more.
The letter also asks the government to ask Enova, a state-owned enterprise that funds the development and adoption of energy and climate technologies, to expand its support schemes to include residential solar systems with battery storage. It then calls for increased support for energy efifcency measures to both Enova and the Housing Bank, suggesting the money comes from either the state budget or Enova’s saved funds.
“Budget negotiations are often about what the parties disagree on. Solar power and energy efficiency, on the other hand, are areas where everyone can win, with measures that can yield gains in a short time,” the letter adds.
Bård Vegar Solhjell, leader of Fornybar Norge, commented that it is “rare” for 16 organisations across the trade union movement, business and the environmental movement to come together around the same demands.
“We agree that more solar power and energy efficiency are good for the power system, energy preparedness and consumers,” he said. “The Storting has also set ambitious goals, but is not following up with the necessary decisions. Now the politicians must use the budget negotiations to do so.”
Norway’s cumulative solar capacity
surpassed 1 GW
recently but the rate of deployment has been declining, with 2026 set to see the lowest annual figure since 2021. Growth has been particularly slow in the residential market, which analysts attribute in part to an optional fixed electricity price for households known as the Norgepris that has removed most of the financial incentive for rooftop solar.
Earlier this month, a group of Green Party politicians recommended
legalising plug-in solar and batteries
in Norway by the end of 2027. Meanwhile, the country’s Energy Regulatory Authority has proposed a
simplified connection process
for small renewable generation facilities it says is designed to make it easier for households, housing associations and other end customers to use PV systems.

title: New multi-modeling approach can predict rice yield in agrivoltaics - pv magazine Global
content:
Research & Development
Researchers in Japan have developed a modeling approach to optimize rice yields and electricity generation in agrivoltaic systems. Their findings show that adjusting solar panel tilt angles can improve crop productivity and help meet regulatory yield requirements, with limited economic losses.
Emiliano Bellini
26 Oct 2026
Research & Development
Cells & modules
Utility-scale
The agrivoltaic testing facility used for the experiments
Maintaining high crop productivity in
rice fields hosting solar panels
remains a major challenge for agrivoltaic projects, as demonstrated by a
recent research project
conducted by the University of Tokyo in Japan. The six-year experiment showed that grain yields reached 8.5 tons per hectare in the control plot, compared with 6.5 tons per hectare in the agrivoltaic field, representing a 23% reduction.
The results confirmed that rice yields in the agrivoltaic system were limited by reduced biomass and fewer panicles, both of which are critical to rice productivity. Grain quality also deteriorated under partial shading, particularly in terms of grain chalkiness and head rice yield.
With these challenges in mind, another research group from the University of Tokyo has proposed a multi-modeling approach that could help accurately predict rice yields in agrivoltaic systems.
“Our study is the first to build a multi-modeling framework that couples three models – solar radiation environment, rice growth and yield, and photovoltaic power generation. It predicts rice yield and electricity output simultaneously in rice agrivoltaic systems,” corresponding author Yoichiro Kato told
pv magazine
. “It integrated radiation, rice growth, and photovoltaic models to jointly predict rice yield and electricity generation under agrivoltaic panels, enabling probabilistic, climate-based design of panel configurations that meet yield targets while quantifying the impact on power output and revenue.”
The researchers used Rhinoceros, Grasshopper and Ladybug Tools to simulate solar radiation reaching rice crops beneath the panels. They used the ORYZA crop model to estimate rice yields under agrivoltaic and conventional cultivation conditions, while PVsyst simulated electricity generation. The models were calibrated and validated using field data collected between 2019 and 2022 at an experimental site in Chikusei, Japan.
The agrivoltaic installation covered 1,416 m2, with a ground coverage ratio of 27% and monthly adjustments to panel tilt angles. The researchers then used 30 years of meteorological data, from 1994 to 2023, to assess long-term crop yields and electricity production.
Transplanting operations at the testing facility
The research group simulated additional panel tilt angles ranging from 10 degrees to 70 degrees to determine how increased sunlight availability could affect rice growth. A key objective was to identify configurations capable of achieving at least 80% of conventional rice yields, in line with Japanese regulations.
The team also calculated the probability of meeting this threshold under different weather conditions. The researchers then assessed the economic implications of optimizing panel tilt angles, considering both rice sales and electricity revenue.
The researchers found that their computer simulations closely matched the results measured during field experiments. The models accurately reproduced sunlight levels, rice growth and electricity generation, suggesting that they could reliably predict the performance of agrivoltaic systems under different conditions.
Simulations based on 30 years of weather data, from 1994 to 2023, showed that rice yields under agrivoltaics averaged 82% of conventional cultivation levels, ranging from 66% to 94%. The probability of falling below Japan’s regulatory threshold of 80% was 26%. Average electricity generation between May and September reached 32,893 kWh, with a coefficient of variation of 7.1%.
The researchers also found that increasing panel tilt angles toward the vertical improved sunlight availability and rice yields, although it reduced electricity production. Increasing the tilt angle by 7 degrees raised the probability of achieving at least 80% of conventional rice yields to 80%, while reducing annual income by just 0.1%.
Adjustments of 30 degrees and 53 degrees increased this probability to 90% and 95%, respectively. These configurations improved rice yields by 4.2% and 10.3%, but reduced electricity generation by 3.2% and 9.4%, respectively. Consequently, annual income declined by 2.7% and 8%, respectively.
“The approach can be extended to other design variables, such as panel size and installation density, as well as to assessments of site suitability based on region, climate and cultivar characteristics,” Kato said.
The researchers presented their findings in “
Balancing crop production and electricity generation in rice agrivoltaic systems: A multi-modeling approach
,” published in
Field Crops Research
“These findings confirmed that the multi-modeling approach, which integrates irradiance, crop, and photovoltaic models, can assess grain yield and electricity generation in rice agrivoltaics, thereby reducing potential risks when exploring different agrivoltaics configurations within the food–energy nexus,” the researchers concluded.
In 2025, another research group from the University of Tokyo investigated whether
agrivoltaic systems based on dual-axis trackers could improve rice productivity
. The experiments showed that, over two growing seasons, rice yields under the panels were 75% and 85% lower than those in nearby benchmark paddies without solar modules. However, the researchers found that yields, while slightly lower in the first year, improved significantly in the second year after they fine-tuned the amount of sunlight reaching the crops.

title: Hungary proposes energy upgrades for single-family homes, apartments - pv magazine Global

Markets & Policy
A government program in Hungary is preparing to offer single-family homes and condominiums non-refundable subsidies and preferential loans for energy efficiency measures including solar PV and heat pump installations.
Patrick Jowett
26 Oct 2026
Applications & Installations
Markets & Policy
Batteries
Energy Storage
Heat pumps
Highlights
Residential
The Hungarian government is preparing a multi-year program to improve the energy efficiency of single-family homes and condominiums as part of its 2027 budget.
Hungary’s Ministry of Economy and Energy, István Kapitány, announced last week a HUF 600 billion ($1.83 billion) budget to support the renovation of 15,000 single-family homes and 15,000 condominiums annually, reaching up to 120,000 families by the end of the decade.
The program would offer beneficiaries non-refundable grants and interest-subsidised loans to cover up to 95% of eligible costs. Single-family homes would be eligible to receive up to HUF 15.5 million ($47,273), while condominiums could receive a maximum HUF 5.2 million ($15,860).
Analysis published by the Hungarian Solar Cell Solar Collector Association (MNNSZ) lists nine eligible activities under the program, including the installation of a solar PV system. The association explains gross billing will apply to new solar PV connections, so using the electricity on site, such as with a heat pump or storage systems, will improve the return on investment.
Heat pump installations are also covered by the proposed package, alongside connection to district heating systems. Other building retrofits including insulation, modern lighting and replacing windows and doors.
Kapitány added the total HUF 600 billion budget could bring at least HUF 1,100 billion ($3.35 million) of orders to the construction industry.
Detailed conditions for the program, including full eligibility and implementation details, are yet to be published. MNNSZ says the launch of the program depends on the adoption of the proposed budget and the plans still under negotiation. It adds the procedure for implementation will be determined by later legislation and a call for applications.
Plans to modernise Hungary’s single-family homes and condominiums form part of a wider package of energy development measures worth HUF 868 billion ($2.65 billion) which also includes plans for network development, wind and geothermal energy, modern metering and energy storage.
MNNSZ says HUF 100 billion ($305 million) worth of EU funds would be allocated to strengthen the electricity grid in 2027 under the proposals, while it is planned to build 3 GW of energy storage capacity by 2030. Hungary’s Prime Minister, Péter Magyar, said the government would provide non-refundable support to 57,000 households to install their own energy storage systems.
Hungary added
of solar last year, taking cumulative capacity to over 8.3 GW.
Earlier this year, the government launched a
residential grant scheme
for battery storage systems, offering up to HUF 2.5 million ($7,820) per household. It recently
extended the deadline
for completing projects under its EU-funded residential solar program to the end of this month following a series of delays.

title: World’s largest artificial reef: Nearly 1,000-foot ocean liner to sink off Florida coast
content: An ocean liner is about to take its final, most improbable voyage: straight to the bottom of the Gulf of Mexico. Okaloosa County officials announced this week that the historic SS United States is slated to be sunk off the Florida coast during the second week of November, weather permitting. The ship that raced across the Atlantic will soon stand completely still, offering ocean life a vast new home. Settling into the seabed roughly 22 nautical miles (41 kilometers) southwest of Destin, the legendary ship is set to become the “world’s largest artificial reef”: a underwater metropolis for marine life. “This is an exciting move forward to create a one-of-a-kind resource for the environment and for our tourism industry,” county officials wrote in a news release as AP reported. County leaders expect the new attraction to draw scuba enthusiasts and charter fleets from around the world, funneling millions of dollars each year into local dive shops, charter fishing outfits, and hotels. Transatlantic record-breaker It is a striking second act for a vessel born of speed and mid-century American ambition. Launched in 1952 , the nearly 990-foot ocean liner shattered the transatlantic speed record on its maiden voyage, cutting across the Atlantic in just three days , ten hours, and forty minutes. This feat shattered the Queen Mary’s previous record by roughly 10 hours. The vessel earned the coveted Blue Riband for the fastest transatlantic passenger liner crossing, a title Atlas Obscura reports the ship still holds today. Reports said building the SS United States cost between $70 million and $79.4 million. The U.S. government funded $50 million of the total sum to help support the ship’s construction. But decades of changing travel habits left the ship docked, rusting, and facing an uncertain future. Retired in 1969 after 17 years at sea, the vessel passed through several owners while steadily deteriorating over the decades. A rent dispute with the owner of its Philadelphia pier eventually forced the SS United States Conservancy to sell the vessel. Okaloosa County purchased the ship for $1 million, leading to its February 19, 2025 departure from Philadelphia under tow to Mobile, Alabama. Preservationists fought for years to restore the grand liner, but astronomical maintenance costs ultimately sank those ambitions. Marine haven Now, its fate lies on the ocean floor. Environmental groups and scientists raised concerns that the vessel’s zinc chromate primer could contaminate the Gulf, though Okaloosa County confirmed the project satisfies EPA regulations. A federal lawsuit attempting to stop the sinking was dismissed in August 2025. County officials described the initiative as an exciting advancement for local tourism and environmental growth. Measuring 990 feet, the ocean liner will surpass the 888-foot USS Oriskany, which held the record for the largest artificial reef since its sinking off Pensacola in 2006. Supporters expect the rusting hull to turn into a thriving reef ecosystem for divers and local marine life. Joining a network of more than 500 existing artificial reefs in the region, the SS United States is expected to become the crown jewel of Gulf Coast diving.

title: US scientists detect incoming drones from 49 feet using motor signals
content: A new passive sensing approach has been designed to detect and identify micro-unmanned aerial systems (micro-UAS/drones) near critical infrastructure. Every electric drone in the sky carries some sort of signature. It isn’t an encrypted radio ping or a flashing LED light, but an invisible, unavoidable hum: the extremely low-frequency (ELF) magnetic field thrown off by its spinning brushless motors.Now, researchers at Florida International University (FIU) have figured out how to use ELF to spot incoming threat drones without firing a single signal into the air.Catching dronesDrones have advanced modern warfare, evolving from high-altitude novelties into cheap, mass-producible airborne weapons. To fight back, the U.S. Department of War requested a $74 billion for drone and counter-drone technologies in its fiscal 2027 budget request. Active radar remains the primary defense against airborne threats, but carries a major vulnerability.Typical active radar, optical, and acoustic systems face constraints from line-of-sight barriers, environmental background noise, and strict transmission regulations. Passive ELF magnetic sensing reduces these vulnerabilities by covertly capturing motor emissions. This technique operates silently, without broadcasting signals. It offers a stealthy detection alternative unaffected by weather conditions or acoustic interference.“Every detection method currently in use gives something away. Radar transmits a signal. Acoustic systems get overwhelmed by background noise. We went a different direction entirely,” said Arjuna Madanayake, an Associate Professor at FIU’s College of Engineering & Computing who led the research. “While the range of our method is limited for now, it costs only a few hundred dollars to develop and could run continuously without any specialized support, unlike radar systems,” Madanayake said. The FIU team converts a basic physical requirement of drone flight into an effective security trap. Different motor configurations across drone models create unique electromagnetic fingerprints, which could help track and identify specific devices. Low-cost fix for drone detectionThe researchers built a specialized circular loop antenna paired with a low-noise analog front end to capture these subtle magnetic waves. And ran the raw signals through a Fast Fourier Transform process to map out spectral correlation patterns, essentially converting raw magnetic hums into distinct visual “maps.”According to the study, a VGG16-based convolutional neural network (CNN) then takes over, reading the maps to decide whether a drone is nearby and what kind it is.In outdoor field tests, the system performed with startling precision. It achieved 98.5 percent outdoor detection accuracy at ranges up to 49 feet (15 meters). And 83.5 percent overall accuracy when classifying four distinct scenarios (three separate drone models plus a no-drone baseline).Although a 49 feet detection range remains modest, the system excels in its stealth and low manufacturing cost. A purely passive receiver emits no signals, making it invisible to hostile forces trying to jam or locate defensive sensors. Electromagnetic fields pass through fog, total darkness, and heavy environmental noise, providing reliable detection where optical and acoustic sensors routinely fail.“Knowing the type of drone that’s coming matters,” Madanayake said. “Different drones can carry different payloads and have different threat profiles. The more you can tell a defender about what’s coming, the better they can respond.” The FIU research group is currently partnering with U.S. industry players to boost the system’s detection range. If scaled successfully, low-cost passive magnetic arrays could soon sit silently around power plants, military bases, and critical infrastructure, listening for the invisible signatures of approaching danger.

title: Watch: 3D-printed scroller write endless text with marbles 58
content: Engineer Ivan Miranda has done it once again. A 3D-printing buff, he’s brought us some wild creations in the past. His most recent one is the scroller that uses black and white marbles to display text. By making it giant and round, Miranda ensured it can keep displaying text endlessly. Whether it’s a text message or a long letter, the scroller can display it all. If you and I had unlimited access to a 3D printer, what would we print? An action figure? A musical instrument maybe? Perhaps even a to-scale model of a bike, car, airplane, or rocket. But this is where YouTubers are different. They don’t think about what one can do in an afternoon or over a weekend. The vision extends over weeks and months, and the final video you see is just a snippet of the work that went on behind the scenes. Interesting Engineering has previously covered Miranda’s builds, and they consisted of a motorbike, go-kart, and even a treadmill. Needless to say, they were not to-scale models but working ones. While these are impressive, Miranda does have a online reputation for building display clocks with marbles, and this time, he has gone above and beyond his previous achievements. Giant ScrollerFor his latest, Miranda has ditched the digits of his digital clocks for text. In theory, if you can do digits, you can do text. The major difference, however, is where and how these letters are displayed. While the digital clock and its variations had to contend with changing numbers, everything happened in a relatively small space. For the scroller, Miranda chose a giant circular design, and while that gives him a large canvas to showcase the text, it also adds immense complexity to the operation. For someone like Miranda, who has been making digital content for over five years, complexity is where things start getting interesting. The solution to solving the complexity challenge is multiple iterations with more 3D-printed parts that we can even imagine and the ease with which they fit into the grand plan of making the device work. How does it work? The scroller consists of a giant circumferential ring which is made up of 3D-printed parts and where the letters are displayed. A few things that are not 3D printed in the structure are ball bearings made of steel and a stepper motor that makes the the wheel move. The crucial component of the entire assembly is the selector arm that decides whether a black marble or a white one needs to be dispatched in a particular direction to make a letter. This arm is also powered by a stepper motor, while an infrared sensor helps it make the distinction between marble colors. The setup also boasts a marble collector that sends marbles that fall off the bottom back into the system. Though made entirely of 3D-printed parts, the full setup is massive and fills Miranda’s workshop. Like with any other engineering project, things do go off sometimes, and letters appear a bit crooked. But with a little help from its human creator, the system returns to displaying large blocks of text endlessly.
